action.unchanged: {name} is still identical to the original. Change and save it to start the experiment or add another variant.
banner.completed: The experiment is complete and it is no longer served.
banner.draft: Once the experiment starts, part of your visitors see it instead of the original.
banner.paused: The experiment is paused: visitors see the original until it resumes.
banner.running: Part of your visitors currently see it instead of the original.
banner.title: You are editing a variant of this entry.
banner.unpublished: It is not published, so visitors keep seeing the original. Publish it to have it served.
banner.unpublished.locale: It is not published in this locale, so visitors keep seeing the original there. Publish it to have it served.
banner.winner: It won the experiment and is served to every visitor.
complete.description: The winner is served to every visitor from now on. Choosing the original ends the test without changing what is served.
complete.title: Complete the experiment
create.name: Experiment name
create.name.hint: Shown in the list of experiments. A copy of this entry is created as Variant B for you to edit.
create.title: Create an A/B test
delete.description: Visitors go back to the original entry. What should happen to the variants?
delete.hint: Visitors go back to the original entry. You choose what happens to the variants.
delete.title: Delete this experiment
dispose.hint: Kept variants become ordinary unpublished entries in the Content Manager.
guide.description: Without abSeed the API always returns the original, so nothing changes until your frontend sends it.
guide.dp.description: A variant is an ordinary entry with its own draft and published versions.
guide.dp.draft: Creating one copies the drafts of the original. Publish it like any entry, per locale. Publishing or unpublishing the original never touches its variants, and the other way round.
guide.dp.draft.title: A variant starts as a draft.
guide.dp.keep: Choosing to keep variants when deleting an experiment unpublishes them, so they stay as drafts in the Content Manager. On a content type without Draft & Publish they become regular entries instead.
guide.dp.keep.title: Kept variants are unpublished.
guide.dp.served: A visitor assigned to a variant that has no published version in the requested locale gets the original, labelled {fallback}. Editing a variant's draft changes nothing for visitors until it is published, and unpublishing a variant sends its visitors back to the original.
guide.dp.served.title: Visitors only get published versions.
guide.dp.start: An experiment cannot start while none of the variants that get traffic is published, or while one of them is still identical to the original.
guide.dp.start.title: Starting needs a published variant.
guide.dp.title: Draft & Publish
guide.i18n.copy: A new variant gets a copy of the original in each of its locales. From there each locale of the variant is edited, translated and published on its own, so a variant can be live in some locales and not in others.
guide.i18n.copy.title: Every locale is copied.
guide.i18n.description: Each variant has its own locales; a locale without a published variant serves the original.
guide.i18n.scope: Experiment settings let you restrict a test to some locales; elsewhere the original is served. Keep a test to the locales where its variants are published, otherwise visitors of the other locales are counted with {fallback} in the label.
guide.i18n.scope.title: Scope the experiment.
guide.i18n.seed: The seed is hashed with the experiment key only, so a visitor who switches language keeps the same version.
guide.i18n.seed.title: One assignment across locales.
guide.i18n.title: Internationalization
guide.label: Served entries carry {param} with the experiment key and the version, "control" for the original. Send it to your analytics tool to compare versions. {fallback} means the variant was not published in that locale and the original was returned.
guide.label.title: Read the label.
guide.measure.compare: Among the visitors exposed to each version, count those who then sent the conversion event: a funnel from the exposure to the conversion, broken down by version. For page views, compare the pages viewed per exposed visitor instead. With PostHog connected, Experiment settings shows this comparison for you.
guide.measure.compare.title: Compare the versions.
guide.measure.conversion: When the visitor completes the action, send the event named in the success metric. It does not need to carry the version: the analytics tool links both events through the visitor. Keep the name you typed and the name your frontend sends identical: a different name counts no conversion.
guide.measure.conversion.title: Report the conversion.
guide.measure.description: The plugin serves versions but counts nothing: your frontend reports to your analytics tool, and versions are compared there.
guide.measure.exposure: When a tested entry is displayed, send an event to your analytics tool with the experiment key and the version from {param}. Send it from the browser, so crawlers are not counted, and skip entries labelled {fallback}. For results to show up in Strapi, name it {event} with the properties {experiment} and {variant}, as in the example.
guide.measure.exposure.title: Report the exposure.
guide.measure.goal: In Experiment settings, before starting: a conversion, with the name of the event that counts as one, or page views. It is what your team agrees to judge the test on, shown in the list of experiments and when picking a winner.
guide.measure.goal.title: Set a success metric.
guide.measure.strapi: It picks a version and labels it. It receives no event and counts no visitor: results are measured by your analytics tool (PostHog, GA4, Plausible…). With PostHog connected, which is optional, the plugin fetches them from there and shows them in Experiment settings.
guide.measure.strapi.title: Strapi only receives the seed.
guide.measure.title: How to measure which version wins
guide.preview: {param} forces Variant B for one request, {control} forces the original.
guide.preview.title: Preview a version.
guide.seed: Add {param} to read requests, REST or GraphQL, with a stable id per visitor. Strapi hashes it to pick a version, so the same visitor always gets the same one and responses stay cacheable. Behind a CDN, send a number from 0 to 99 instead of a unique id to cap cache variations.
guide.seed.title: Send a seed.
guide.title: How to serve variants from your frontend
leave.description.experiment: {name} has no saved change. If you leave this page, it is deleted, and so is the experiment.
leave.description.variant: {name} has no saved change. If you leave this page, it is deleted.
leave.hint: To keep it, stay on this page, change something and save.
leave.hint.publish: To keep it, stay on this page, change something and save. Saving is enough to keep it, but visitors only get it once it is published.
leave.title: Leave {name} unchanged?
modal.goal.conversion: Conversion: visitors who complete an action
modal.goal.event.hint: The event your frontend sends to your analytics tool when a visitor completes the action.
modal.goal.hint: What decides the winner. The plugin records it; you read the results in your analytics tool, or here once PostHog is connected. Settings → A/B Testing explains both.
modal.goal.hint.connected: What decides the winner. Its results are read from PostHog and shown above.
modal.goal.pageviews: Page views: pages viewed per visitor
modal.hypothesis.hint: What you expect this test to show, and why.
modal.locales.hint: Leave empty to run in every locale. A locale where a variant is not published serves the original.
modal.name: Name
modal.remove-variant.description: The variant leaves the experiment. What should happen to its entry?
modal.remove-variant.title: Remove this variant
modal.schedule.error: The end must be after the start.
modal.schedule.hint: Optional. Outside these dates a running experiment serves the original.
modal.split.error: Variants cannot add up to more than 100%.
modal.title: Experiment settings
page.column.name: Experiment
page.empty: No experiment yet. Enable a content type in Settings → A/B Testing, then open an entry and create a variant.
page.subtitle: Experiments are created from an entry in the Content Manager, with "Create a variant".
page.title: A/B Testing
panel.empty: Create a variant of this entry to test a different version with part of your visitors.
panel.title: A/B test
picker.label: A/B test version
plugin.name: A/B Testing
posthog.card: Shows the results of your experiments in Strapi.
posthog.convention.exposure: Named {event}, sent when a tested entry is displayed, with two properties taken from the {label} label of the entry: {experiment} and {variant}. Under any other name, or without these properties, the visitor is not counted.
posthog.convention.exposure.title: One exposure event.
posthog.convention.goal: A conversion is counted when PostHog receives an event with exactly the name typed in the success metric of the experiment. Page views are counted from the {pageview} events PostHog records.
posthog.convention.goal.title: The event of the success metric.
posthog.convention.heading: What your frontend must send
posthog.convention.title: Results only show up if your frontend follows this convention exactly:
posthog.convention.visitor: PostHog links the exposure and what follows through the visitor, so send both with the same PostHog client. A visitor counts once, for the first version seen, and only for what happened after seeing it.
posthog.convention.visitor.title: The same visitor for both.
posthog.description: Optional. A/B testing works without it: your frontend reports to the analytics tool of your choice and you compare versions there. With a PostHog project connected, the plugin reads the results of each experiment from PostHog by itself and shows them in Experiment settings: visitors, conversions, difference with the original and significance, for the success metric of the experiment.
posthog.example.description: An example with made-up numbers, for an experiment whose success metric is a conversion. Each version gets its visitors, its conversions, the difference with the original and how reliable that difference is.
posthog.example.heading: What you get in Experiment settings
posthog.form.key.hint: It starts with phx_. Create it in PostHog, under Settings → Personal API keys, with the "Query Read" scope. The project token (phc_…) your frontend uses cannot read results.
posthog.form.key.hint.saved: A key is saved ({hint}). Leave empty to keep it, or paste another one to replace it.
posthog.form.note: The key is checked with PostHog when you connect, stored encrypted, and never shown again.
posthog.form.project.hint: The number in the address of your project: us.posthog.com/project/12345.
posthog.form.title: Connection
posthog.from-config: This connection is set in {file}, which takes precedence over this page. Change it there.
posthog.project: Results are read from project {project} on {host}.
posthog.title: Results from PostHog
results.draft: Results appear here once the experiment has started.
results.empty: PostHog has no exposure for this experiment yet. Your frontend must send the ab_test_exposure event with the experiment and variant properties: see Settings → A/B Testing.
results.no-goal: Set a success metric below and save: PostHog results are read for that metric.
results.note: Read from PostHog at {time}. A visitor counts once, for the first version seen, and only for what happened after seeing it. Treat a difference as reliable from 95% significance.
results.title: Results from PostHog
settings.content-types.empty: Create a collection type first: A/B testing works on collection types of your application.
settings.integrations.hint: Optional. A/B testing works without them: connect one to see the results of your experiments in Strapi.
settings.subtitle: Choose which content types can be A/B tested.
settings.title: A/B Testing
settings.uninstall.confirm: Every experiment is deleted and visitors get the original entries. What should happen to the variants?
settings.uninstall.description: Variants are regular entries that the plugin keeps hidden. Removing the package without cleaning up would make published variants appear as separate entries. This removes every experiment and these settings first.
settings.uninstall.done: {experiments} experiment(s) removed. The plugin can now be uninstalled.
settings.uninstall.title: Prepare for uninstall
